verdict.rationale: Lindy's own docs say you can describe a process once in natural language and Lindy saves it as a reusable skill it invokes automatically, which covers generating a workflow from a prompt. Routines add scheduled or triggered automation, but the evidence never shows routines being authored from a prompt. Missing for 10: documented editing or refining of an existing skill or routine via prompt, detail on how a described process becomes a structured workflow, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can generate or edit a workflow from a natural-language prompt

citations.quote: Describe the process once, and from then on Lindy picks the right skill whenever a request calls for it.
It saves the process as a skill and uses it from then on.
Lindy routines turn your recurring work into hands-off automation — set a schedule or trigger once, and Lindy runs the whole job for you on autopilot
